successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: southern Powys, which continued as a marcher lordship (the Lordship of Powis) after 1284

ledger.x: 1160: Powys splits and the southern half is the future Powys Wenwynwyn under Owain Cyfeiliog.
1197: Gwenwynwyn seizes the cantref of Arwystli.
ledger.cp: Arwystli (previous holder not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1208: John arrests Gwenwynwyn and Llywelyn annexes southern Powys.
1215: Gwenwynwyn is restored to his realm and makes Welshpool his capital.
1216: Llywelyn defeats Gwenwynwyn and drives him out of southern Powys again.
1241: Gruffudd ap Gwenwynwyn returns and is invested with southern Powys.
1284: the Statute of Rhuddlan ends the Welsh principalities; southern Powys becomes a marcher lordship.
1284: the princely state of Powys Wenwynwyn ends; the land continues as the Lordship of Powis to 1309.

wars.name: Llywelyn the Great's annexation of southern Powys
wars.outcome: John arrested Gwenwynwyn in October 1208 and Llywelyn annexed southern Powys; Mathrafal was destroyed in 1212; Gwenwynwyn was restored in 1215 and defeated by Llywelyn in 1216, dying in England that year; the 1218 Treaty of Worcester confirmed Llywelyn's…

wars.name: Edward I's conquest of Wales
wars.outcome: Gruffudd ap Gwenwynwyn returned to English protection 'after 1276' following a failed plot against Llywelyn; his soldiers helped kill Llywelyn ap Gruffudd near Builth in 1282 and mobilised in the Welsh War of 1282-1283; the principality ended in 1283-1284.

certainty.note: The cantref boundaries are approximate and no treaty line is on the pages; the Welsh-English frontier on the Severn and Vyrnwy (Shropshire) is unsurveyed.
